text.p: The Indian global depositary market closed little changed in London.
"There are market holidays starting on Friday and going on through next week so this market is set for not a lot of anything," said a trader.
Some Indian markets close Friday for the Dhan Teras festival and Diwali takes place next week.
The HSBC James Capel Indian GDR index closed up 0.31 points at 60.41 points, with the premium over the local market at 13.01 percent compared with yesterday's 12.58 percent.
The Bombay Stock Exchange 30-share index fell 18.68 points to 3,0441.16.
EIH Ltd, formerly East India Hotels, net profit rose to 474.3 million rupees in the six months to September 30 from 399.0 million a year ago.
Its shares were quoted at $17.50/$18.50 after a capitalisation issue.
"The results were in line, nothing to get excited about," said the trader.
ITC, which is embroiled in a dispute over alleged violations of India's Foreign Exchange Regulation Act, fell 25 cents to $7.50/$8.50.

The Capel Korea GDR Index ended little changed, up 0.09 point at 65.03, a premium of 26.05 percent over the local market after the Korea Composite Index rose 13.59 points, or 1.85 percent, to a provisional close of 747.24.

The Capel Taiwan GDR Index rose 1.18 points, 1.31 percent, to 91.01, a premium of 1.29 percent over the local market after the Taiwan Weighted Index rose to a 1996 high with a 49.51 points rally, or 0.75 percent, to 6,653.65. -- David Chance London newsroom 44 171 542 5887
